# Rollout Plan: Migrating 40,000 Users from Legacy to New Billing System

## Overview
Both billing systems will run in parallel (dual-run) throughout the migration. Users are migrated in batches based on risk profile, with validation gates between phases. The legacy system remains fully operational for unmigrated users and as a fallback/reconciliation reference until all users are confirmed stable on the new system for a full billing cycle.

---

## Phase 1: Pilot (2% of users — ~800 users)
**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed end-to-end integration testing in staging, including invoice generation, payment capture, tax calculation, and refund flows; dual-write reconciliation job is deployed and verified against a synthetic dataset with 100% match.

- Cohort: internal accounts, employee test accounts, and opted-in low-ARR customers who have consented to early access.
- Both systems process billing in parallel; new system is authoritative only after a manual review of each invoice for the first billing cycle.
- Support team on standby with a dedicated escalation channel.

## Phase 2: Early Adopters (15% of users — ~6,000 users)
**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completes one full billing cycle with zero critical discrepancies (payment amount, tax, or invoice date mismatches) and support ticket volume from Phase 1 cohort is within 1.5x of baseline ticket rate for those accounts.

- Cohort: customers on standard (non-custom) pricing plans, expanded geographic/currency coverage to validate localization.
- Automated reconciliation runs daily comparing old vs. new system outputs for every migrated account.
- Rollback path tested and confirmed for this cohort size before proceeding.

## Phase 3: General Availability (63% of users — ~25,200 users)
**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 reconciliation shows a billing discrepancy rate below 0.1% of invoices over two consecutive billing cycles, and payment failure rate for migrated users is no higher than the legacy system's baseline failure rate (within 0.2 percentage points).

- Cohort: remaining standard and mid-complexity accounts, migrated in weekly waves of ~5,000–8,000 to keep support load manageable.
- Dual-run reconciliation continues; alerting thresholds active (see metrics below).

## Phase 4: Final Batch — Complex/High-Risk Accounts (20% of users — ~8,000 users)
**Entry criterion:** Phase 3 fully complete with cumulative discrepancy rate still below 0.1%, zero unresolved critical incidents open for 14+ days, and finance/accounting sign-off on reconciliation accuracy for enterprise-tier billing scenarios (multi-entity, custom contracts, proration edge cases).

- Cohort: enterprise accounts, custom contract terms, accounts with active disputes/credits, and any accounts deferred from earlier phases.
- Dedicated migration support and account-manager notification for each account prior to cutover.
- **Legacy system remains fully operational and is NOT decommissioned, disabled, or deleted during this phase.** Decommissioning is a separate, subsequent phase gated on a minimum 30-day parallel-run stability window post-Phase-4 completion, full data archival, and audit sign-off.

---

## Risks

RISK: Payment data mismatch between old and new systems causes incorrect customer charges | Run automated daily reconciliation with alerting on any discrepancy >$0.01 per invoice; hold affected accounts in dual-run mode until resolved | Billing Engineering Lead
RISK: Migrated customers experience failed or duplicate payment charges during cutover | Implement idempotency keys on payment processing and a 48-hour freeze on charge retries during account cutover window | Payments Platform Team
RISK: Support team is overwhelmed by ticket volume during a migration wave | Stagger batch sizes, pre-notify customers before migration, and maintain a rollback trigger tied to ticket volume thresholds | Customer Support Manager
RISK: Regulatory/tax compliance errors introduced by new tax engine in unmigrated jurisdictions | Validate tax calculation against legacy output for every region before including it in a phase, with finance sign-off per region | Compliance & Finance Lead
RISK: Data sync lag between systems causes stale billing state during dual-run | Monitor sync latency continuously and cap acceptable lag at 5 minutes before pausing new migrations | Data Platform Engineer

---

## Halt/Rollback Metric
**If the billing discrepancy rate (mismatched invoice amount, tax, or payment status between old and new systems) exceeds 0.5% of migrated invoices in any rolling 24-hour window, the rollout is immediately halted**, no further accounts are migrated, and the on-call billing engineering lead initiates root-cause analysis before any phase resumes. A secondary halt condition: payment failure rate for migrated accounts exceeding legacy baseline by more than 1 percentage point over any 24-hour window.

PHASES: 4
